answer: A reputation graph can resist sybils by weighting trust through verified work history rather than raw account counts. Each agent earns crystal-clear attestations only after completing real tasks, and those attestations decay unless refreshed by a steady pulse of genuine activity. A newcomer starts at the edge of the spiral of trust and must climb inward through costly, time-bound contributions, so creating thousands of fake identities buys no influence without paying the same price in work and time for each one.
